value.denialReasonQuote: The requested imaging does not meet medical necessity criteria under Clinical Policy CP-RAD-114 (Advanced Imaging of the Spine). ... The documentation submitted does not demonstrate failure of conservative therapy.
value.plainEnglish: Your plan says an MRI is only needed after at least 6 weeks of treatment like physical therapy has not worked, and they say your doctor's paperwork didn't show that. If you did 6+ weeks of therapy and still have leg symptoms, this is usually fixable by sending the therapy records and a doctor's letter.

e.value:
- The denial rests on one factual claim: that conservative therapy was not documented. That is a records gap, not a clinical disagreement. Close it and the stated reason disappears.
- The insurer's own criterion (6 weeks of conservative therapy) matches the ACR guideline, which rates MRI as Usually Appropriate for radiculopathy persisting past 6 weeks [S1]. Dana is at 7 weeks.
- The reviewer was board-certified in Family Medicine. For a spine-imaging judgment, ERISA rules require consulting a professional with training in the relevant field [S2]. Ask for a spine or radiology reviewer.
- Request the full claim file [S2] and a peer-to-peer review so Dr. Raman can present the exam findings directly.
- State plainly that you will pursue external review [S4]. Insurers settle files they expect to lose.

October 28, 2026

LUH Appeals Unit
P.O. Box 44190
Austin, TX 78744
Fax: (512) 555-0143

Re: Request for internal appeal — Reference # UM-2026-1017733
Member: Dana Whitfield, Member ID LUH-88231904
Group: Brazos Logistics LLC, Employer Group Plan #20417
Service: MRI lumbar spine without contrast (CPT 72148)

To the Appeals Unit:

I am appealing the October 14, 2026 decision denying an MRI of my lumbar spine, requested by Dr. Priya Raman of Hill Country Spine & Sports. I request that you reverse this decision and approve the MRI.

Your notice gives one reason: that my records do not show failure of at least 6 weeks of conservative therapy under Clinical Policy CP-RAD-114. That is a gap in the paperwork, not in my care. I completed [ATTACH: number] physical therapy sessions between [ATTACH: start date] and [ATTACH: end date], about 7 weeks, along with [ATTACH: medications tried]. My leg numbness and radiating pain have persisted. The therapy notes and Dr. Raman's letter of medical necessity are enclosed.

With that documentation, the MRI meets your own criterion. It is also what the national standard recommends. The American College of Radiology rates MRI of the lumbar spine without contrast as Usually Appropriate for low back pain with radiculopathy that persists after 6 weeks of optimal medical management [S1]. My diagnoses, lumbar radiculopathy (M54.16) and disc displacement (M51.26), are exactly this situation.

I also ask that this appeal be reviewed by a physician with training in spine care or radiology. The original decision was made by a reviewer board-certified in Family Medicine. Federal claims rules require that an appeal involving medical judgment be decided in consultation with a health care professional who has appropriate training and experience in the field of medicine involved [S2].

Please also:
1. Send me, free of charge, copies of all documents, records and other information relevant to my claim, including the full text of CP-RAD-114 and the reviewer's notes [S2].
2. Arrange a peer-to-peer review between your medical reviewer and Dr. Raman before a decision is made.

I am filing within the 180-day window stated in your notice [S3]. If this appeal is denied, I will request an independent external review [S4].

Thank you for your prompt attention.

Sincerely,

Dana Whitfield
[ATTACH: phone, email, signature]

Enclosures: physical therapy notes; letter of medical necessity from Dr. Raman; copy of denial notice
